sentences.en: MAYA: So, Finn, I've done as much as I can for our project on theatre programmes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 好了，芬恩，关于我们关于戏剧节目单的项目，我已经尽我所能完成了。

sentences.en: How's your research coming along?
sentences.zh: 你的研究进展如何？

sentences.en: FINN: OK, Maya.
sentences.zh: FINN: 好的，玛雅。

sentences.en: I didn't know theatre programmes are called playbills in the USA till I started looking into the topic.
sentences.zh: 直到我开始深入研究这个主题，我才得知戏剧节目单在美国被称为‘演出广告单’（playbills）。

sentences.en: Even though I struggled to find man: y useful websites, I'm glad we picked this subject.
sentences.zh: 尽管我费了不少劲才找到许多有用的网站，但我很高兴我们选了这个课题。

sentences.en: No one else on the course is doing the same as us, although it is one of the research areas of the module convener.
sentences.zh: 课程上没有其他人做和我们相同的课题，尽管这恰好是本模块负责教师的研究领域之一。

sentences.en: MAYA: That might actually put some people off.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 这反倒可能让一些人望而却步。

sentences.en: FINN: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我想确实如此。

sentences.en: Anyway I hadn't realised there are actually companies specialising in creating theatre programmes
sentences.zh: 不过，我之前根本没意识到，居然真有公司专门从事戏剧节目单的设计与制作。

sentences.en: MAYA: Yes they are quite common nowadays.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，如今这类公司已相当普遍。

sentences.en: Contrary to what man: y people think, theatres don't hire people to do the programmes.
sentences.zh: 与许多人所想的相反，剧院并不会雇人来制作节目单。

sentences.en: In fact, companies buy the rights to publish programmes on the theatre's behalf and then make their money selling advertising space within the programme booklet.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些公司会向剧院购买授权，代表剧院出版节目单，然后通过在节目册内出售广告位来盈利。

sentences.en: FINN: It must be easier for theatres to do it that way.
sentences.zh: FINN: 对剧院来说，这样操作肯定更简便。

sentences.en: MAYA: Yes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 没错。

sentences.en: FINN: I remember reading something about programmes in early British theatre.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我记得曾读到过有关英国早期戏剧节目单的内容。

sentences.en: It said that the cast was always very important.
sentences.zh: 文中提到，演员阵容始终至关重要。

sentences.en: MAYA: Yeah, audiences were very familiar with leading actors and big names would draw huge crowds.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是啊，观众对当红主演和知名演员都非常熟悉，大牌明星往往能吸引大量观众。

sentences.en: FINN: But I hadn't realised that if the programme named a famous actor, that's who the public expected to perform.
sentences.zh: FINN: 但我之前并不知道，只要节目单上列出了某位著名演员的名字，公众就理所当然地认为此人一定会登台演出。

sentences.en: And if that didn't happen, people accused the theatre of breaking their agreement with the audience.
sentences.zh: 倘若实际演出并非如此，人们便会指责剧院违背了与观众之间的约定。

sentences.en: They would demand refunds and if they didn't get them, there were riots.
sentences.zh: 他们要求退票；若得不到退款，甚至会爆发骚乱。

sentences.en: MAYA: Outrageous!
sentences.zh: MAYA: 太离谱了！

sentences.en: That'd never happen now.
sentences.zh: 现在这种情况绝不可能发生。

sentences.en: FINN: No, people are too polite, even when they're disappointed if the star of the show misses a performance.
sentences.zh: FINN: 不会的，人们太有礼貌了，即便对演出主角缺席感到失望，也依然如此。

sentences.en: MAYA: We should definitely include that information about early audiences in our project.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我们在项目中一定要包含早期观众的这些信息。

sentences.en: I also think it's important to mention that lots of ordinary people at that time were illiterate, so theatre programmes were of limited value in advertising plays.
sentences.zh: 我还觉得有必要提到，当时许多普通民众都是文盲，因此戏单在宣传戏剧方面作用十分有限。

sentences.en: When a company of actors arrived in a town, they'd parade around the streets in their costumes, beating drums and announcing their upcoming performances.
sentences.zh: 当一个剧团抵达某座城镇时，他们会身着戏服在街头游行，敲打鼓点，并宣布即将上演的剧目。

sentences.en: FINN: Interesting.
sentences.zh: FINN: 很有意思。

sentences.en: I couldn't imagine that happening now either.
sentences.zh: 我也无法想象现在会发生这种事。

sentences.en: MAYA: There's also an interesting comparison to make between 18th and 19th century programmes.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 此外，18世纪与19世纪的戏单之间还有一个有趣的对比。

sentences.en: FINN: Wasn't it in the 19th century that theatre programmes started to resemble programs today
sentences.zh: FINN: 剧场戏单不就是在19世纪开始变得与当今的节目单相似的吗？

sentences.en: MAYA: Yes and unlike programs from the 18th century they always used colour
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，而且与18世纪的戏单不同，它们始终采用彩色印刷。

sentences.en: FINN: And there was a greater variety of designs.
sentences.zh: FINN: 并且设计样式也更加丰富多样。

sentences.en: But personally I think 18th century programmes were superior because they told the theatregoers so man: y things, including about the actors.
sentences.zh: 但就我个人而言，我认为18世纪的戏单更胜一筹，因为它们向观剧者提供了大量信息，包括有关演员的信息。

sentences.en: MAYA: And about the writer, the plot and sometimes the history of the play.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 还有关于剧作家、剧情，有时甚至包括该剧历史的信息。

sentences.en: FINN: That's right.
sentences.zh: FINN: 没错。

sentences.en: What should we say about theatre programmes in the 20th century?
sentences.zh: 关于20世纪的剧场戏单，我们该说些什么呢？

sentences.en: MAYA: I reckon the most important thing is the dramatic change they underwent during World War II.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我认为最重要的是它们在第二次世界大战期间所经历的剧烈变化。

sentences.en: FINN: When the government imposed restrictions on the use of paper.
sentences.zh: FINN: 当时政府对纸张使用实施了限制措施。

sentences.en: MAYA: Yeah, but that was only in the UK.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 是的，但那仅限于英国。

sentences.en: In the USA, programmes, or rather playbills, continued to be published in the same format.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，戏单——或者说演出广告单——则继续以原有格式出版。

sentences.en: FINN: While here in the UK, programmes became merely a single sheet of paper folded to create four pages for text.
sentences.zh: FINN: 在英国期间，节目单简化为一张纸对折后形成四页文字。

sentences.en: MAYA: What I don't really get is that after the war they didn't go back to being more than one sheet or change in any way for over 25 years.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我不太明白的是，战后它们并未恢复为多页形式，而且在长达25年的时间里也未作任何改变。

sentences.en: I know there were paper shortages after the war, but only for five or ten years.
sentences.zh: 我知道战后确实存在纸张短缺问题，但仅持续了五到十年。

sentences.en: FINN: Strange.
sentences.zh: FINN: 真奇怪。

sentences.en: MAYA: I got some pictures of programmes we could include on the slides for our presentation.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 我找了一些节目单的照片，我们可以把它们放进演示文稿的幻灯片里。

sentences.en: FINN: I found a couple too Maya.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我也找到了几张，玛雅。

sentences.en: Let go through and see what we think
sentences.zh: 我们一起来看看，挑出我们认为合适的。

sentences.en: MAYA: Um oh this is an old one for a play called Ruey Blass
sentences.zh: MAYA: 嗯……哦，这是一份很老的节目单，是为一部名为《鲁伊·布拉塞》的戏剧制作的。

sentences.en: FINN: Never heard of that.
sentences.zh: FINN: 这部戏我从来没听说过。

sentences.en: But the programme looks very decorative.
sentences.zh: 但这本节目单看起来装饰性很强。

sentences.en: MAYA: Good enough to put in a frame on the wall.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 足够精美，完全可以装进相框挂在墙上。

sentences.en: The images are just beautiful.
sentences.zh: 这些图片实在太美了。

sentences.en: Finn, what did you find?
sentences.zh: 芬恩，你找到了什么？

sentences.en: FINN: I've got some pages from a programme for Man: of La Man: cha.
sentences.zh: FINN: 我找到了几页《堂吉诃德》的节目单。

sentences.en: I thought this was a good programme to show, not because of the pictures, but because it contains articles written by members of the theatre company, so we can learn how the production was created and the thoughts and feelings of the cast.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这份节目单很适合作为展示材料，倒不是因为其中的图片，而是因为它收录了剧团成员撰写的文章，因此我们可以了解该剧的创作过程以及演员们的所思所感。

sentences.en: MAYA: Good.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 很好。

sentences.en: I've got a copy of a programme that's now in a museum.
sentences.zh: 我还有一份如今收藏于博物馆中的节目单。

sentences.en: It's for The Tragedy of Jane Shore and it's said to be the earliest surviving document to have been printed on Australia's first printing press
sentences.zh: 这是为《简·肖尔悲剧》制作的节目单，据称是澳大利亚第一台印刷机印制的现存最早的文献。

sentences.en: FINN: Fantastic!
sentences.zh: FINN: 太棒了！

sentences.en: MAYA: Another programme to talk about is for The Sailors Festival.
sentences.zh: MAYA: 另一份值得讨论的节目单是《水手节》的。

sentences.en: It comes from the British Library's digitised collection of programmes that was started a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 它源自大英图书馆几年前开始的节目数字化收藏。

sentences.en: It already comprises over 200,000 programmes which is amazing!
sentences.zh: 目前已收录了超过20万档节目，这简直令人惊叹！

sentences.en: FINN: Huh.
sentences.zh: FINN: 嗯。

sentences.en: Wish I'd known about it while I was doing my research.
sentences.zh: 真希望我在做研究时就知道它的存在。
